terms.comment: cēnātōrius “for dinner” is post-Augustan (Petronius, Martial, of dinner clothes).

phrases.latin: Suntne currus cēnātōrius et currus dormītōrius in hōc trāmine?
phrases.english: Are there a dining car and a sleeping car on this train?

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 211, 216, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
